publisherRightsChecks.scope: Bounded checks of actual relevant source pages and a small set of reusable-photo candidates, not an exhaustive publisher-wide search.

publisherChecks.result: The public plans page describes purchase of individual picture licences. It is not a public reuse grant, and no photo licence was purchased or otherwise obtained. Each original candidate retains its separate unresolved rights record.

publisherChecks.inspection: Actual article text and DOM image inventory read in cloud browser. The article image is a logical-sandbox diagram; remaining image elements were related-story cover artwork. Image bytes were not downloaded.
publisherChecks.result: No documentary photograph was identified on the actual announcement page. No asset-specific reuse grant was established for the diagram; it was not copied or redrawn. A separately generated conceptual illustration is used. No conclusion is made about all OpenAI imagery.

publisherChecks.inspection: Actual article read in web search and cloud browser; complete main image inventory contained three related-story artwork cards, not incident photos.
publisherChecks.result: No documentary incident photograph identified on this actual primary-source article. Generic public-domain cybersecurity event photographs are considered separately below. A clearly labeled incident-response concept illustration was chosen rather than misrepresenting a past meeting as an incident scene.

publisherChecks.inspection: Actual announcement and complete image inventory read in cloud browser. One 300×195 asset observed.
publisherChecks.result: The actual announcement image inventory exposed only a 300×195 Cabinet Office-named asset; no documentary photograph of the announced AI lab was established. Its full pixels, photographer and capture date were not verified, so it was not selected as a cover. The site-wide OGL footer was not treated as automatic asset-specific clearance. A labeled conceptual illustration avoids implying a verified physical laboratory scene.

Verified file-page PD-US-FCC notice, but subject is an old small-business cybersecurity roundtable with inconsistent date fields (2011 description versus 2009 camera date). Not the present incident-response subject; no full pixel download or adoption. Rejected for relevance and date ambiguity, not lack of an open licence.

File page describes a still from a US NIAID laboratory video, unknown date, with public-domain rationale and a warning that NIAID can also use commercial images. The pictured US BSL-4 cabinet is not the new UK AI institution; it was not downloaded or adopted. Rejected for relevance and incomplete per-image provenance, not a blanket copyright conclusion.

Asset-specific CC BY 2.0 grant, Jakub Mosur attribution and Commons historical Flickr review established. Original bytes visually inspected and adopted as a dated 2010 archival equipment photo. This grant is separate from any current Bloom press-kit terms.

W.carter, 29 December 2018, CC0 photo acquired and inspected. Not adopted because the very dark foggy night composition is less legible as a cover than the selected oil tanks. A rights-cleared alternative is not misreported as a rights failure.

note: Four individually verified archival photographs, including one body-only tanker rendition, and three clearly labeled AI-generated editorial illustrations. All seven are independently selected replacements. Six covers must reuse their identical files in corresponding article bodies. No original Reuters bytes were delivered or acquired. Original-page read failures, missing pixels and unestablished rights are separately audited. No data charts were generated or recreated.
